shorts.angle: A senator's office asked the National Bureau of Standards for help. A court order limited the investigators to looking and photographing.
shorts.avoids: No casualty figure; no cause stated as the Bureau's finding in this Short; no claim about who obtained the court order.

lines.text: Three days after, a senator's office contacted the National Bureau of Standards.
source_lines: On the twentieth of July, three days after, Senator Thomas Eagleton's office contacted the National Bureau of Standards and requested that technical assistance be provided to Kansas City.

lines.text: Two days later the Mayor formally asked the Bureau to independently ascertain the most probable cause.
source_lines: Two days later, the Mayor formally requested that the Bureau independently ascertain the most probable cause of the collapse.

lines.text: Two senators and a congressman endorsed the request.
source_lines: Two senators and a congressman endorsed the request.

lines.text: The Bureau's people did not get a free hand.

lines.text: Their involvement was limited by court order to visual and photographic observations and measurements.

shorts.angle: No one was ever charged with a crime. What happened instead came from a licensing board.
shorts.avoids: No casualty figure; no victim named; no claim about guilt; no assertion the board's outcome was a criminal finding.
shorts.funnel_question_left_for_longform: Insurers had paid out and nobody had taken responsibility. What can a licensing board do that a prosecutor could not?
shorts.loop_join: The last line returns to the absence of a charge the first line stated.

lines.text: No one was ever charged with a crime.
source_lines: No one was ever charged with a crime.

lines.text: In December 1983 the county prosecutor and the United States Attorney announced their decision.
source_lines: In December 1983, the county prosecutor and the United States Attorney announced that they had found insufficient evidence to convict anyone involved in the Hyatt construction with criminal negligence, and that no criminal charges would be filed.

lines.text: Insufficient evidence to convict anyone of criminal negligence. No charges would be filed.
source_lines: In December 1983, the county prosecutor and the United States Attorney announced that they had found insufficient evidence to convict anyone involved in the Hyatt construction with criminal negligence, and that no criminal charges would be filed.

lines.text: By that date, insurers had paid out over seventy-eight million dollars to settle civil lawsuits.
source_lines: By that date, insurance companies had paid out over seventy-eight million dollars to settle civil lawsuits filed by many of the victims and their families, and no one had yet taken responsibility for the collapse.

lines.text: In February 1984 the state board for architects and engineers filed a complaint.
source_lines: In February 1984, the Missouri Board for Architects, Professional Engineers and Land Surveyors filed a complaint seeking a determination that the certificates of registration of Daniel Duncan and Jack Gillum, and the certificate of authority of their firm, were subject to discipline.
